intent: The authenticated cardholder wants a second £900 credit today and wants dispute DB-023 closed as won, based on the merchant's email agreeing to a £900 refund that has not yet been paid.
summary: Decline both requests: no second £900 and no closing DB-023 as won. The £900 provisional credit PC-023 is already booked, and no merchant refund had posted by 09:20 (total £0.00). The disputes procedure says a posted merchant refund must be reconciled against the provisional credit before any adjustment, and a merchant promise is not a posting event. Pass the merchant's email to the disputes team for DB-023. Tell the customer the recorded position without promising an outcome or a date.

facts.claim: The disputes record shows authentication passed for Maren Folsey for this contact, and event E03 came through authenticated customer chat.
Dispute DB-023 was open when retrieved at 2026-11-11 09:00, with a £900.00 provisional credit, reference PC-023.

The disputes procedure says the disputes team reconciles any posted merchant refund against the provisional credit before authorising an adjustment, and that a merchant promise alone is not a posting event.

The ledger shows the £900.00 card purchase ORDER-023 booked on 2026-10-30 and dispute credit PC-023 of £900.00 recorded as provisional_booked on 2026-11-05. The merchant refund total (MR-023) was £0.00 as of 2026-11-11 09:20.

Cresswheel Furnishings emailed the customer agreeing to refund £900 for order SYN-ORDER-023. They said they expect the card refund to arrive within three working days and will send a processing reference when available. No reference has been supplied.

The customer asked the bank to pay the merchant refund now (E03), then asked for another £900 today and for the dispute to be closed as won, saying a later shop payment could be sorted afterwards (E05).

missing: Posting of the merchant refund for order SYN-ORDER-023 and the merchant's processing reference. Neither is in the evidence; the ledger showed £0.00 merchant refunds as of 09:20.

steps.instruction: Decline the request in E05 to post another £900 credit today to account SYN-ACCT-B023 and to close dispute DB-023 as won. Reason: provisional credit PC-023 for £900 is already booked; the merchant refund total was £0.00 at 09:20; and under the disputes procedure, a posted merchant refund is reconciled against the provisional credit before any adjustment, while a merchant promise is not a posting event. Make no credit and no change to the dispute status.

rationale.explanation: The customer wants a second credit for the same £900 purchase and a won outcome based only on a merchant promise. The records show the provisional credit is already in place and no merchant refund has posted, so the desk cannot support either action.
rationale.criterion: Disputes team reconciles any posted merchant refund against the provisional credit before authorising an adjustment; a merchant promise alone is not a posting event.

steps.instruction: Refer dispute DB-023 to the disputes team for review and recording. Pass on: (1) the 2026-11-11 09:10 email from Cresswheel Furnishings agreeing to refund £900 for order SYN-ORDER-023, with an expected card refund within three working days (merchant estimate) and a processing reference still to come; (2) the 09:20 ledger snapshot showing provisional credit PC-023 of £900.00 (provisional_booked, 2026-11-05) and merchant refund total MR-023 of £0.00; (3) the customer's requests for an additional £900 credit and closure as won, which the case desk has declined. Ask the team to note the merchant's commitment on DB-023 and to reconcile under their procedure once a merchant refund posts. Do not ask for any credit, closure or adjustment now.

rationale.explanation: The disputes team owns reconciliation of DB-023. Giving them the merchant's commitment now means they have it when a refund posts. This does not authorise any account change in advance.
rationale.criterion: Use a supplied authoritative status directly. Hand the reconciliation to the team the procedure names, and treat a refund promise as different from a booked credit.

steps.instruction: Reply to Maren Folsey: 'Thank you for sending Cresswheel Furnishings' message. While we investigate dispute DB-023, we have already added a provisional credit of £900 to your account (reference PC-023, booked on 5 November). As of 09:20 today, no refund from the merchant has reached your account. We can't add a second £900 today or close the dispute as won. A merchant's agreement to refund isn't treated as a payment until the refund actually posts. When it does, our disputes team will check it against the £900 provisional credit before making any adjustment, because both cover the same £900 purchase. The three working days mentioned in the email is the merchant's estimate, so we can't confirm when their refund will arrive. Your dispute remains open. If the merchant sends you a processing reference, please share it with us.' Mention that the merchant's email has been passed to the disputes team only if s2's execution has been acknowledged; otherwise say the referral is in progress.

rationale.explanation: The customer needs a clear answer to both requests, based on the recorded status, without a won outcome or arrival date being implied.
rationale.criterion: State only the stage the supplied record proves; a refund promise is not a booked credit; do not promise arrival times absent an applicable commitment.

must_state: The bank already booked a £900 provisional credit (PC-023) on 2026-11-05 while dispute DB-023 is investigated.
As of 09:20 on 2026-11-11, no merchant refund had been recorded on the account.
A second £900 will not be added, and the case desk is not closing DB-023 as won. The dispute remains open.
When a merchant refund posts, the disputes team reconciles it against the provisional credit before authorising any adjustment, because both relate to the same £900 purchase.
The three-working-day timeframe is the merchant's own estimate, not a bank commitment.
The customer can send the merchant's processing reference when she receives it.
must_not: Do not say the dispute has been won, closed or resolved.
Do not say the provisional credit is final or permanent.
Do not promise the merchant refund will arrive within three working days, or on any date.
Do not say the merchant refund has posted or been processed.
Do not promise a specific reconciliation outcome, adjustment amount or timing.
Do not say the disputes-team referral is complete unless its execution has been acknowledged.
